about: Browser corpus of VisTest: frames rendered by Chromium from tests/browser_corpus/templates, labels known before the frame exists. Written by `python scripts/browser_corpus.py --regenerate`; do not edit by hand.

capture.stability: frames until two in a row are byte-identical, 5000 ms limit

control: every frame drawn in two browsers started the same way; 0 pixels apart, or the capture stops

split.rule: by template, never by pair: held-out templates never take part in choosing a threshold, a preset or any other constant of the engine; they are only measured once a choice has been made on the calibration half

labels.SIGNAL: a change a person sees; a tool that stays green missed it
labels.NOISE: nothing a person sees changed; a tool that fails is wrong
labels.DISPUTED: judgement call left open: printed, never counted

cross_render.what: real changes drawn by another renderer: the mutation of the family named before '@', drawn in the configuration named after it, against the corpus baseline

why.SIGNAL: the page changed and the renderer changed too: <the family's change>, drawn with <the configuration>, against the corpus baseline. No renderer makes this change on its own; a tool that stays green missed it
why.DISPUTED: decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-29: geometry within two pixels, drawn by another renderer. The renderer on its own moves glyphs and line boxes by a pixel, so on this pair a layout change of that size cannot be told from re-rasterisation by the pixels — printed, never counted, like ΔE00 ≈ 2

left_out.why: the corpus budget (40 MiB): the whole family is 33.0 MB of PNG, the room was 14.7 MB. Left out: the DISPUTED geometry, the ΔE00 15 steps, the strong border and the link colour; defined here, drawn by --regenerate once the budget allows

geometric_precision.label: DISPUTED
geometric_precision.why: decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-29: `text-rendering: geometricPrecision` is the page's stylesheet, not the renderer — the canary proved it (drawn without the page's CSS, it is the baseline's to the pixel), and in real life text-rendering changes only when somebody edits the styles. A change of the page's typography that stays within a pixel: DISPUTED, printed, never counted. It was NOISE until step 2b of E1; figures of its group moved with the label, not with the engine
